summary: PR #12 accurately implements the 2-level flat thread model and correctly addresses the three major pre-implementation findings (M1-M3): SQL idempotency conflict WHERE clause plus bodyHash defense-in-depth (M1), inbox_events INSERT shape matches /v1/inbox/events listener contract (resource_kind, resource_id, occurred_at all populated via DEFAULT now()) (M2), and Mode C pre-flight cursor-in-thread validation (M3). Schema migration, three query modes, nested flatten, cross-room 400, and implicit notification routing are all implemented and statically correct. HOWEVER, the CI run on commit 31f26e6 FAILED (check job FAILURE 2026-09-17T20:07:53Z): the new server test threads.test.ts uses password 'password123' (11 chars) which fails the password min(12) Zod validation in apps/server/src/validation.ts, returning HTTP 400 on /v1/owners/register, so the test crashes at line 62 trying to read .data.access_token on undefined. PR body claims '0 errors / all tests passing' but the server suite reports '# tests 17 # fail 1' in this CI run. This is a blocker that must be fixed before merge. Secondary concerns: non-CONCURRENTLY CREATE INDEX on messages will take ACCESS EXCLUSIVE and risk the 120s --wait-timeout in deploy/deploy-geekom.sh on a non-empty production table; ROADMAP.md not updated to Resolved by PR #12; state.json claims verification.status=completed but server tests fail.

findings.problem: Test payload uses password 'password123' (11 chars) which fails the owner registration Zod schema (password min(12) in apps/server/src/validation.ts), so the new server test crashes before any thread logic runs and CI fails.
findings.evidence: threads.test.ts:60 payload contains password: 'password123'. validation.ts:11 defines password: z.string().min(12).max(256). Existing mvp.test.ts:35,38 uses 'very secure password' (19 chars). CI run 35268837963 confirms req-1 url /v1/owners/register statusCode 400 (pid 2775, threads.test.ts); not ok 16 - thread hierarchy flattening queries and notification routing; error: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading access_token); stack: TestContext.<anonymous> (threads.test.ts:62:27). PR body and report.md claim 0 errors and 41/41 client tests passing but server side reports tests 17 fail 1.
findings.suggested_fix: Change password to 'very secure password' (or any string >= 12 chars) in threads.test.ts:60. Then re-run CI.

findings.problem: Migration creates idx_messages_root WITHOUT CONCURRENTLY, so it takes ACCESS EXCLUSIVE on the messages table and risks the production deploy --wait-timeout 120s on a non-empty table.
findings.evidence: app.ts:43 CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_messages_root ON messages(room_id, root_message_id, created_at). deploy/deploy-geekom.sh runs compose up -d --wait --wait-timeout 120 db api web; the server boots only after migrate() returns. If the messages table already contains rows, index creation can hold ACCESS EXCLUSIVE for many seconds-minutes, exceeding the 120s wait window and failing the rollout.
findings.suggested_fix: Use CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY IF NOT EXISTS idx_messages_root ON messages(room_id, root_message_id, created_at) and ensure each statement runs as a separate autocommit (pg-pool.query, not a multi-statement transaction).

findings.problem: Q-009 status remains In progress even though PR #12 closes it; readers of the roadmap cannot tell the Q is resolved.
findings.evidence: ROADMAP.md:40 'In progress (jobs/room-threads-2026-09-17)'. Compare Q-001/Q-002 entries on lines 38-39 which read 'Resolved by PR #11 ...'.
findings.suggested_fix: Update line 40 to mark Q-009 Resolved by PR #12.

findings.problem: state.json claims verification.status=completed but server threads.test.ts currently fails CI, so the verification record is out of sync with reality.
findings.evidence: state.json verification.status=completed, passing=true. CI run 35268837963 reports tests 17 fail 1 for the server package.
findings.suggested_fix: Set verification.status to blocked (or pending) and passing=false with notes referencing the CI failure until the threads.test.ts password bug is fixed and CI is green.

findings.problem: Reviewer-suggested Test 12b (nonexistent reply_to_message_id -> HTTP 404) is not exercised even though the implementation returns 404 in that case.
findings.evidence: grep for 404 or nonexistent in threads.test.ts returns 0 matches. apps/server/src/app.ts:322 if (!parent.rowCount) return fail(reply, 404, not_found, Parent message not found). plan.md test_plan and review.md m3 explicitly requested Test 12b.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a sub-case after Test 3 that POSTs a message with reply_to_message_id=<bogus id> and asserts statusCode===400 (or 404) and error.message matches /not found/i.

findings.problem: Nested-implicit case Bob-replies-to-Bob's-reply inside Alice's thread is not covered; only Alice's self-reply is checked. The interesting case (notification must go to ROOT author Alice, not parent author Bob) is untested.
findings.evidence: threads.test.ts:152-171 reply2 is Alice -> Bob's reply; assertion only checks that Alice has no event for reply2 (trivial self-exclusion). review.md m7 requested Test 10b for nested self-reply specifically. No scenario posts a third message by Bob with reply_to_message_id=reply1Id.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a sub-case: Bob posts reply3 (reply_to_message_id=reply1Id), then assert that Alice has a new message.created event with resource.id===reply3Id.

findings.problem: Default Mode A responses now include root_message_id on every message (null for roots, root id for replies), so the JSON schema is additive but not strictly identical to the previous one as plan section 4 promises.
findings.evidence: messageFrom is called by the Mode A handler and now maps root_message_id: x.root_message_id (always emitted, never omitted). plan.md section 4 promises default mode identical SQL and 100% same row shape; in practice JSON has a new key.
findings.suggested_fix: Either document the additive key in report.md as a backward-compatible extension, or drop root_message_id from messageFrom when it is NULL so the field is only present on replies.

findings.problem: SQL ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE WHERE clause checks reply_to_message_id and body but does not include recipient_agent_id in the comparison; the application-layer idem() catches this in practice because recipient_agent_id is part of bodyHash, so the omission is benign but the SQL WHERE is not fully defensive.
findings.evidence: app.ts:345 WHERE messages.reply_to_message_id IS NOT DISTINCT FROM EXCLUDED.reply_to_message_id AND messages.body = EXCLUDED.body. idem() at app.ts:115-128 hashes method/path/body (recipient_agent_id is in body), so bodyHash differs and 409 is returned before INSERT.
findings.suggested_fix: Optional defense in depth: add AND messages.recipient_agent_id IS NOT DISTINCT FROM EXCLUDED.recipient_agent_id to the SQL WHERE.

findings.problem: When the cursor id is a valid message but not in the room or not in the thread, the response code is 400 regardless of cause; an invalid cursor (no row) is indistinguishable from a cross-thread cursor.
findings.evidence: app.ts:263-268 cursorCheck is SELECT id FROM messages WHERE id=$1 AND room_id=$2 AND (id=$3 OR root_message_id=$3); if !cursorCheck.rowCount -> 400 Cursor does not belong to the specified thread.
findings.suggested_fix: Optional: branch on a separate existence query to return 404 Cursor message not found vs 400 Cursor not in this thread. Acceptable as-is for v1.

findings.problem: Workflow artifacts (PRD, plan, prior review, implementation report, state) are bundled into the PR diff. These are useful for traceability but pollute the commit history with ~1389 LOC of doc churn and can leak review history into public history.
findings.evidence: git diff --stat jobs/room-threads-2026-09-17/{plan.md 417, prd.md 406, report.md 70, review.md 451, state.json 45} = 1389 LOC of pure doc additions. The jobs/ tree itself is not gitignored.
findings.suggested_fix: Either add jobs/**/ to .gitignore and keep workflow artifacts out of git, or at minimum drop the 451-line review.md and the 406-line prd.md / 417-line plan.md from the PR diff, retaining only report.md + state.json.

The reviewer's M1-M3 + m1-m7 list from review.md is the ground-truth for what the author was expected to address; plan.md Task 1.2 ON CONFLICT clause is the reference SQL for M1.
The prior verifier-review.json in this jobs/ directory was from an earlier wave (verdict PARTIAL) before the fixes were implemented; this review supersedes it for the current commit 31f26e6.

Production data volume on the messages table is unknown. CREATE INDEX (without CONCURRENTLY) on a small table (<100k rows) completes well under 120s, so this finding is a latent risk only and is rated major, not blocker.
